_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present
entries.usage: The imperfect: now or habitual.
entries.example: أدرسُ العربية.

entries.label: Past
entries.usage: A finished past action.
entries.example: درستُ أمس.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: سـ / سوف + present.
entries.example: سأدرسُ غدًا.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: After أن / لن — the naṣb ending.
entries.example: أريد أن أدرسَ.

entries.label: Jussive (لم)
entries.usage: لم + jussive negates the past.
entries.example: لم أدرسْ.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: اُدرسْ!

entries.point: Derived verb forms II–IV (فعّل، فاعَل، أفعَل)
entries.label: Forms II–IV
entries.usage: Derived patterns that shift meaning.
entries.example: علّم، قاتل، أرسل

entries.point: Derived verb forms V–X (تفعّل، انفعل، افتعل، استفعل)
entries.label: Forms V–X
entries.usage: More derived patterns.
entries.example: تعلّم، استقبل

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: The action done, doer unnamed.
entries.example: كُتِبَ الدرسُ.

entries.label: kāna (was)
entries.usage: Puts a sentence that has no verb into the past: the weather is nice becomes the weather was nice.
entries.example: كان الطقس جميلًا أمس. — The weather was nice yesterday.

entries.label: Object pronouns
entries.usage: For him, her, me or them stuck onto the end of the verb instead of standing as a separate word.
entries.example: الكتاب مفيد، قرأته كله. — The book is useful; I read all of it.

entries.label: Maṣdar
entries.usage: Naming the activity itself rather than doing it — reading, studying, travelling.
entries.example: القراءة مفيدة للعقل. — Reading is useful for the mind.

entries.label: Participles
entries.usage: Naming the one who does it (a writer) or the thing it was done to (written).
entries.example: هو كاتب مشهور في الصحيفة. — He is a famous writer at the newspaper.

entries.label: Weak verbs
entries.usage: Verbs holding a و or ي that gets shortened or dropped in some forms, so they never look quite regular.
entries.example: القطار يصل في الموعد دائمًا. — The train always arrives on time.

entries.label: Negation (لا / ليس)
entries.usage: For saying not: لا in front of a verb, ليس when the sentence has no verb.
entries.example: لا أشرب القهوة ولستُ جائعًا. — I don't drink coffee, and I'm not hungry.

entries.label: Conditionals
entries.usage: For if — if you study you will pass — and for what would have happened but never did.
entries.example: إذا درست بجد نجحت في الامتحان. — If you study hard, you'll pass the exam.

entries.label: Literary discourse
entries.usage: The joins of written Arabic: as for this…, and the little words that stress something really did happen.
entries.example: أما الطلاب فمجتهدون، وأما المعلمون فمخلصون. — As for the students, they are diligent; as for the teachers, devoted.

entries.label: Sound plurals
entries.usage: Regular masculine and feminine plurals.
entries.example: مُعلِّم → مُعلِّمون

entries.label: Broken plurals
entries.usage: Irregular internal-change plurals.
entries.example: كتاب → كُتُب

entries.label: Dual
entries.usage: Exactly two: -ān / -ayn.
entries.example: كتابان، كتابين

entries.label: Iḍāfa
entries.usage: X of Y by pairing two nouns.
entries.example: بابُ البيتِ

entries.point: The definite article ال — sun and moon letters
entries.label: The article ال
entries.usage: the — with sun/moon assimilation.
entries.example: الشمس، القمر

entries.label: Comparative
entries.usage: The afʿal pattern.
entries.example: أكبر، أجمل

entries.label: Pronouns
entries.usage: The words for I, you, he and she — with one you for a man and a different one for a woman.
entries.example: أنا طالب. — I am a student.

entries.label: Feminine ة
entries.usage: Words for a woman or girl usually end in ة, so most job and role words come as a pair.
entries.example: هي معلمة. — She is a teacher.

entries.label: Demonstratives
entries.usage: For pointing something out — this book, that city — choosing the form that fits the word you point at.
entries.example: هذا كتاب. — This is a book.

entries.label: Adjective agreement
entries.usage: A describing word comes after the thing it describes and copies its endings, so the two match.
entries.example: البيت الكبير قريب. — The big house is nearby.

entries.label: Root & pattern
entries.usage: Most words are built by pouring three letters into a shape, so كتاب, كاتب and مكتب all say something about writing.
entries.example: الكاتب يكتب في المكتب. — The writer writes in the office.

entries.label: Possessive endings
entries.usage: For saying whose something is by adding an ending to the thing owned: my book, your book, her car.
entries.example: هذا كتابي. — This is my book.

entries.label: Numbers 3–10
entries.usage: For counting three to ten of something, where the number takes the opposite ending to the thing being counted.
entries.example: عندي ثلاثة كتب على الرف. — I have three books on the shelf.

entries.label: Zero copula
entries.usage: There is no word for is or are in the present, so the two halves simply sit side by side.
entries.example: الطالب مجتهد. — The student is hardworking.

entries.label: Questions
entries.usage: Put the question word first — what, who, where — or open with هل for a yes-or-no question.
entries.example: ما اسمك؟ — What is your name?

entries.label: Prepositions
entries.usage: The small placing words — in, on, from, to, with — which change the ending of the word after them.
entries.example: الكتاب على الطاولة. — The book is on the table.

entries.label: inna & sisters
entries.usage: Openers like indeed, that, but and because, which change the ending of the word right after them.
entries.example: إنّ الطقسَ جميلٌ اليوم. — The weather really is nice today.

entries.label: Relative الذي
entries.usage: For hanging a description on a known thing: the man who works here, the book that I read.
entries.example: الرجل الذي يعمل هنا طبيب. — The man who works here is a doctor.

entries.label: The ḥāl
entries.usage: Says how someone was while the main thing happened: came running, drank the coffee hot.
entries.example: دخل المعلم الصف مبتسمًا. — The teacher entered the class smiling.

entries.label: The tamyīz
entries.usage: Says what a vague amount or comparison is actually about: filled with water, richer in money.
entries.example: امتلأ الإناء ماءً. — The vessel filled with water.

entries.label: Exception (إلّا)
entries.usage: For leaving one thing out of the whole: everyone came except one.
entries.example: حضر الجميع الاجتماع إلا مديرَهم. — Everyone attended the meeting except their manager.

entries.label: Vocative يا
entries.usage: For calling out to someone with يا, and for insisting that something certainly will happen.
entries.example: يا أيها الطلاب، انتبهوا جيدًا. — O students, pay close attention.

entries.label: Focus fronting
entries.usage: Moves the important word to the front of the sentence, or narrows it down to only that one.
entries.example: هذا الرأيَ لا أقبله. — This opinion, I do not accept.
